technique_name: Inter-Board Communication Transverse Movement > Cross-board communication > Horizontal movement of inter-communication between service boards and between service boards and the main control board.
description: Attackers tamper with terminal software to send specially crafted abnormal protocol packets. They exploit vulnerabilities in service boards to implant malicious code. Then, through inter-board communication messages, they intrude other boards, thereby expanding the attack impact. In extreme cases, attackers can use this channel to attack the main control board, gaining control over the main control board and further intruding the network management system to control the entire network.
potential_defenses: Segment service boards from main control board
code_examples_patterns: Send crafted protocol packets via compromised terminal to exploit service board vulnerability

technique_name: Platform Service Lateral Movement > Lateral Movement on the K8s Platform > Accessing the K8s API via a Service Account
description: An attacker inside a container can access the Kubernetes (K8s) API through a Service Account. The attacker can then probe the current pod user permissions. If the permissions allow, the attacker can issue commands through the API or exploit Kubernetes privilege escalation vulnerabilities to access other resources within the cluster.
privileges_required: Container-level access with Service Account token
resource_required: Service Account token mounted in pod
potential_defenses: Split external-facing and sensitive pods into separate privilege levels
detection_opportunities: Unusual API Server access from pod Service Accounts
Privilege escalation attempts via API calls
code_examples_patterns: Use mounted Service Account token to query K8s API and enumerate cluster resources

technique_name: Platform Service Lateral Movement > Lateral Movement on the K8s Platform > Accessing the K8s Dashboard
description: After discovering the service address where the dashboard is located, the attacker, in the event of improper configuration of administrative permissions, issues commands through the K8s Dashboard.
privileges_required: Container-level access with Service Account token
potential_defenses: Restrict K8s Dashboard access with RBAC
Disable Dashboard in production if not needed
Enforce authentication and authorization on Dashboard
code_examples_patterns: Access K8s Dashboard with stolen credentials to execute commands on cluster

technique_name: Platform Service Lateral Movement > Lateral Movement on the K8s Platform > Attacking a Third-Party K8s Plugin
description: If the platform deploys third-party Kubernetes plugins with misconfigurations and vulnerabilities, these insecure configurations and the use of third-party Kubernetes plugins/tools will introduce new attack surfaces and provide entry points for lateral movement.
privileges_required: Container-level access with Service Account token
potential_defenses: Avoid deploying unvetted third-party K8s plugins
Conduct security audits before deploying plugins
detection_opportunities: Plugin network traffic to external endpoints
code_examples_patterns: Exploit misconfigured third-party K8s plugin API to gain cluster access

technique_name: Platform Service Lateral Movement > Lateral Movement on Cloud Platform > Stealing Credentials Attack on Cloud Services
description: Attackers exploit internal container files or communication credentials of cloud services obtained from K8s secrets to perform lateral movement and access cloud service APIs.
privileges_required: Compromised container or pod with credential access
resource_required: K8s secrets or cloud credential files
detection_opportunities: Cloud API calls using stolen credentials
code_examples_patterns: Extract cloud credentials from K8s secrets and use to access cloud service APIs

technique_name: Platform Service Lateral Movement > Lateral Movement on Cloud Platform > Stealing credentials to attack other applications
description: In scenarios where infrastructure is highly containerized, the vast majority of services are API-based. This makes credential theft a critical method for expanding the attack surface and obtaining target data. Communication credentials for K8s clusters, cloud products, and self-built applications are all targets for attackers to steal.
privileges_required: Compromised container or pod with credential access
resource_required: K8s secrets or cloud credential files
detection_opportunities: Cloud API calls using stolen credentials
code_examples_patterns: Extract cloud credentials from K8s secrets and use to access cloud service APIs

technique_name: Application Layer Service Horizontal Movement > Lateral Movement of Internal Network Services within a Cluster > Internal Network Penetration within a Cluster
description: A Kubernetes cluster forms an environment similar to an internal network. Attackers can use internal network penetration techniques to discover services of other pods and perform lateral movement.
